blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
It is natural to associate the finite spectrum of fundamental particles to a finite quantum space endowed possibly with some additional structure. This point of view underlies, with some variations, most noncommutative geometric approaches to particle physics (see e.g. [@mdv-ker-mad:1989a], [@mdv-ker-mad:1988b], [@mdv:1991], [@ac-lot:1990], [@cha-ac:1997], [@cha-ac-mar:2007]). Such a finite quantum space is a virtual space associated to its algebra of observables that is a finite-dimensional real algebra which is a quantum analog of a finite-dimensional algebra of real functions.\

blocks.content: The space of internal states of a quark is the 3-dimensional complex space $\mathbb C^3$ acted by the color group $SU(3)$. blocks.title: The 3 generations and the triality in J83
blocks.content:
As recalled in Section 3.2 of [@mdv:2016b] and originally analyzed in [@jor-vn-wig:1934], the algebra of observables of a finite quantum space should be a finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra which is clearly not the case of the octonion algebra $\mathbb O$.\
However, as pointed out in Section 3.1 of [@mdv:2016b], the existence of three generations of fundamental fermions reveals a sort of triality underlying the classification of these fundamental fermions. Discussion
The advantage of the approach of this paper to the correspondence triality-
generations with respect to the one of [13] is that here one does not need
the introduction of new fundamental fermions and that the formulation of
the electroweak symmetry is straightforward. This new approach which is
based on the key observation that the Euclidean Jordan algebra J8
2 can be
associated with a complete generation seems to be the most appealing one.
